verdict.rationale: Marqeta's agentic-AI MCP Server guide lists instant-issue virtual cards and spend controls (velocity limits, spending caps, merchant restrictions). The Core API documents authorization controls that lock spending to specific merchants and velocity controls that cap amounts. However, the docs frame this as agents operating the platform rather than explicitly naming an agent as the cardholder, and no card expiry control is shown. Missing for 10: documented card expiry or time-bound validity, explicit vendor documentation of issuing a card to an AI agent as the cardholder, and hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can give an agent its own card — issue a scoped virtual card to an AI agent with merchant locks, amount caps, and expiry so autonomous purchases stay inside policy, a use the vendor documents by name

citations.quote: Virtual card issuance: Create instant-issue virtual cards that are ready for immediate use.
Spend controls: Set customizable velocity limits, spending caps, and merchant restrictions.
An authorization control limits spending by specified users at specified merchants. You can limit spending at a single merchant or at a group of merchants
You can configure velocity controls to limit how much users can spend and the number of transactions they can make in a given span of time.
